UnitStatement: Phase C4 GUI slice (TP-C4-CHECKGUI-001) tests: jsdom has no Tauri runtime, so the run route pins the honest browser-preview seam (explicit desktop-only diagnostic, no synthesized fallback) by default; backend-path tests opt in by setting __TAURI_INTERNALS__ and mocking invoke.
deriveRuleCheckBindingPlan partitions a rule pack's required inputs by source kind (solver_result, user_supplied_rule_value, private_library_value) and collects value slots.
deriveRuleCheckBindingPlan falls back to TBD dimension and TBD unit_ref, and uses the input id as the name, when quantity metadata is absent.

classifySolverResultReference returns 'resolves' when the authored result id is present, 'result_missing' when result rows exist but the id is absent, and 'no_result_rows' when no solved result rows are available.
runRuleChecks reports the desktop-only unavailable route ('unavailable_browser_preview') in browser preview with no Tauri runtime, and does not call invoke.
runRuleChecks omits empty binding arrays when invoking run_rule_checks so the backend treats absent bindings as unsupplied (never a silent pass).
runRuleChecks forwards non-empty solver-result and supplied-value bindings and prefers a solved envelope over the model so the backend does not re-solve.
loadDemoRuleCheckPack loads the bundled invented demonstration pack (rule_pack_id 'invented_demo_rule_pack', grammar_version 1.0.0) with a runnable binding-plan shape.

Rule-check runner seam (Phase C4, TP-C4-CHECKGUI-001): running a rule pack's checks against a solved model routes through the desktop (Tauri) run_rule_checks command backed by core/rules/rule_check_runner; browser preview has no backend and reports an explicit unavailable route instead of synthesizing a fallback evaluator.

The rule-check runner emits ONLY the three automatic rule-check statuses and makes no professional, certification, sealing, authentication, approval, or code-compliance claim (PRD §12.5, §22.4; DEC-022 grammar v1.0.0).

RuleCheckStatus is one of three automatic statuses: RULE_INPUTS_INCOMPLETE, USER_RULE_CHECKED, USER_RULE_FAILED. The wider vocabulary (MODEL_INCOMPLETE, MECHANICS_SOLVED, HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED) and the external HUMAN_APPROVED_FOR_PROJECT record are not producible here.
SolverResultSelector binding is caller-supplied because the schema carries no selector tying a solver_result required input to a solved result row, per the rule_check_runner contract.

runRuleChecks prefers an already-solved envelope (so the backend does not re-solve) and falls back to the model so the backend solves it; projectId scopes the private-library lookup for private_library_value inputs (resolved backend-side from the local store).

loadDemoRuleCheckPack returns the invented non-engineering demonstration rule pack (DEL-06-05), byte-parallel to backend fixture examples/rule_packs/invented_demo.yaml; it is NOT an engineering design basis and is not suitable for professional reliance.
LibraryValueRef references a value in a saved private library record, resolved backend-side from the local store at run time and never embedded in the rule pack (IP boundary).
SolverResultRef references a row in the current solved result envelope; authored references are canonical and the run-panel selector is used only for older packs without this member.

RuleCheckBindingPlan: solverInputs bind to a solved result row; valueInputs and valueSlots take a user-entered value plus unit (dimension from the pack); private-library inputs are surfaced separately and treated as unsupplied (never a silent pass).

deriveRuleCheckBindingPlan iterates required_inputs, routing solver_result kinds to solverInputs, private_library_value kinds to libraryInputs, and all other kinds to valueInputs, then collects value_slots.
SolverResultReferenceResolution is one of: 'resolves', 'result_missing', 'no_result_rows', classified by classifySolverResultReference against the solved result rows.

Rule-pack backend seam (Phase C2, TP-MAC-147): validation, checksum computation, and local persistence route through the desktop (Tauri) commands backed by core/rules; browser preview keeps drafts in memory only and reports an explicit unavailable route instead of synthesizing a TypeScript fallback engine.
Private rule packs persist in the local SQLite store only and are never transmitted or committed (OPS-K-PRIV-1, PRD §17.3).

validateRulePack invokes the Tauri validate_rule_pack command with the document and a publicExportRequested flag, returning a RulePackDocumentValidation; in browser preview it returns the unavailable route.
computeRulePackChecksum invokes the Tauri compute_rule_pack_document_checksum command and returns a RulePackComputedChecksum.

saveLocalRulePack invokes the Tauri save_local_rule_pack command with projectId and document, returning a LocalRulePackEnvelope; openLocalRulePack, listLocalRulePacks, and deleteLocalRulePack route through their respective Tauri commands.

draftPlaceholderProvenance returns placeholder provenance for draft authoring surfaces; every field is invented non-engineering wording or TBD, never a copied source, standards citation, or code value (PRD §12.4, IP boundary).

buildDraftRulePackDocument builds a 'New draft rule pack' that is private by default (PRD §12.4); every placeholder is TBD or invented non-engineering wording and the editor never prefills code equations or standards values (PRD §14.5).

A draft rule pack's formula declaration uses declaration_form 'declarative_ast' in the frozen open_pipe_stress_declared_expression grammar (DEC-022 v1.0.0) with arbitrary_code_execution_allowed false and protected_content_policy private_user_owned_reference_only.

A draft rule pack's professional_boundary asserts the software makes no compliance, certification, sealing, approval, or authentication claim; human review is required and project reliance requires separate human review bound to current model, report, and rule-pack hashes.
stampChecksumIntoDocument returns a new document with the computed checksum stamped in (verification_status 'verified', hash_basis 'Canonical JSON/JCS-compatible'), leaving other members untouched.
unitCatalogService reports an explicit browser-preview unavailable route (diagnostic UNIT-CATALOG-DESKTOP-ONLY) instead of synthesizing units when no Tauri runtime is present.

loadUnitCatalog loads the reviewed DEC-018 unit catalog via the Tauri get_unit_catalog command in desktop mode, with storage_convention 'entered_units_preserved' and a boundary asserting no protected content and no professional-approval claim.

describeUnitBasis maps model-unit fields against the reviewed catalog: a canonical match yields a 'DEC-018 canonical' label, a catalog miss yields 'catalog mismatch', and the browser-preview route yields 'model metadata' without inventing browser units.

A UnitCatalogEntry transform_kind is one of identity, multiplicative, or affine; provenance is one of si_canonical, exact_public_definition, conventional_public_constant, or project_governed_decision.

UnitCatalog declares calculation_basis 'si_canonical' and storage_convention 'entered_units_preserved' with a boundary describing protected-content, private-data, professional-approval, and code-compliance exclusions.

loadUnitCatalog returns an unavailable_browser_preview route with UNIT-CATALOG-DESKTOP-ONLY diagnostic when no Tauri runtime is present, otherwise invokes get_unit_catalog; browser preview does not synthesize a fallback catalog.
acceptedUnits filters a unit catalog to entries whose review_status is 'accepted'.
unitCatalogEntryForSymbol matches a catalog entry by normalized symbol and dimension, preferring an accepted entry over any matching entry.
describeUnitBasis produces a UnitBasisDisplay distinguishing catalog_loading, browser_preview_model_metadata, dec018_catalog_accepted, dec018_catalog_unreviewed, and dec018_catalog_miss sources.

dimensionMatches treats requested dimensions as equivalent to catalog dimensions: displacement↔length, stress↔pressure, rotation↔angle, slope↔dimensionless, linear_stiffness↔force_per_length, volume_per_length↔area.
usePackageHash is a React hook keyed on stable JSON text of the packet; canonicalization and hashing happen inside the wasm engine (H1 / F-5a) and the frontend no longer canonicalizes anything.

withCanonicalPackageHash stamps the computed package hash into a packet's manifest and validation_report, marking status computed_local_preview_sha256 when present or TBD_browser_preview_does_not_emit_canonical_package_hash when absent.
loadWasmEngine loads the wasm32 build of core/model_operations/operation_applier — the sole browser-mode operation engine per DEC-020 / ADR-0001.

The wasm glue and artifact are produced by 'npm run build:wasm' into public/wasm-engine/ and are not committed; an absent artifact is an explicit named failure (WASM-ENGINE-ASSET-ABSENT) with the build command, never a silent fallback because no other engine exists.

WasmOperationEngine exposes validateOperationJson, applyOperationJson, and the H1/F-5a hash seam (canonicalJsonString, canonicalSha256Hex) so the frontend never re-implements canonicalization or hashing; both hash functions throw on invalid JSON (WASM-ENGINE-INPUT-JSON-INVALID).

The browser wasm import must be a fully-qualified URL resolved against location.href, not a root-absolute path, because Vite's dev transform refuses to serve publicDir files with the ?import query (HTTP 500); the helper skips URLs carrying a protocol.

Under Node/Vitest, locateAssetsUnderNode probes deterministic candidate paths for the generated wasm assets and fails loudly listing every probed path; this probes one artifact set and is not an engine fallback.
loadWasmEngine is a lazy singleton: the first caller triggers instantiation and failures are not cached, so a later call after 'npm run build:wasm' succeeds.

The OpenPipeStress desktop shell stylesheet (TP-APP-R2-UXSHELL-001) is structured as base+chrome, workspace layout (modeling-workspace and workspace-dock), panel primitives, and feature panels in source order.

Stylesheet layout invariants: every scroll container is a .workspace-pane, the .workspace-dock-body, or an explicitly bounded panel region; panels grow with content instead of clipping, and form rows wrap rather than overflow.
The persistent spatial core (PRD 14.1) is a three-column grid: model tree (280px) | viewport (flexible) | inspector (380px), via the .modeling-workspace rule.
Inactive workspace-dock sections stay mounted so state survives navigation but are fully hidden (display:none), including from the accessibility tree.

The Vitest setup pre-warms the wasm operation engine (DEC-020 / ADR-0001) so jsdom suites that exercise the edit loop start with the engine ready; an absent artifact fails the suite loudly with the build command (WASM-ENGINE-ASSET-ABSENT → 'npm run build:wasm --workspace apps/desktop'), with no fallback engine.
